content.title: How Michigan crushed Arizona in men’s Final Four to reach NCAA Tournament national title game
content.text: Wolverines destroy WildcatsMichigan dominated Arizona in the men’s Final Four, winning 91-73 tonight to advance to the NCAA Tournament championship game.The Wolverines will face UConn on Monday night for the title. Michigan will be seeking its second championship in program history (1989).Aday Mara led a balanced Michigan attack with 26 points, while Trey McKenney came off the bench to score 16. Five Michigan players scored in double figures, and Elliot Cadeau had a double-double with 13 points and 10 assists. Share your thoughts on the games: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMonday night's odds Getty ImagesBoth Michigan and UConn got off to hot starts in Saturday’s Final Four games. The Huskies had to endure a push from Illinois while the Wolverines ran away from Arizona. Considering Michigan’s dominant play, it’s no surprise the Wolverines are big favorites for Monday’s national championship game.Michigan is favored by 7.5 points on DraftKings, BetMGM and FanDuel. The Wolverines opened as a 6.5-point favorite on FanDuel, but that number quickly moved so that all three sportsbooks showed matching odds.May praises Mara Imagn ImagesDusty May on Aday Mara (26 points, nine rebounds and three assists): 💬 “Aday was sensational.”“He was at the rim, catching lobs. He was a force down low. He was a pressure release up top. I mean, he’s such a smart basketball player, and obviously, his rim protection, he did a great job on (Koa) Peat. He did a great job forcing a lot of those misses around the basket because of his aggression.”Trey McKenney on Michigan’s hot start: 💬 “During the season we have had like some type of mental lapses during big games, but I think we came out, and we really knew how high the stakes were, and we just really wanted to leave it all on the floor. We had nothing left.“Really, we only have a couple of days left with the bonds that we’ve made throughout the summer.”Michigan transfer stars heap praise on coaching staff Imagn ImagesElliot Cadeau (UNC transfer) and Aday Mara (UCLA transfer) spoke to how Dusty May and the Michigan coaching staff integrated a team of four transfers (this season) in a short period of time:Cadeau: 💬 “I think they did a really good job putting four transfers, or five players on the court at all times that are really good at passing the ball. I think they knew that when they were recruiting all of us, just having five people on the court that are all playmakers and also great scorers just helps us have connectivity on the court, for sure.”Mara: 💬 “I think the same. They did a great job putting, as he said, players that were not selfish. And I think now in the era we are with the transfer portal, we’ve just got to learn and adapt as soon as possible to what we have and the different teams that we play. So I think just we’ve got to change and we’ve got to learn every day so we can play together.”Lloyd to TucsonTommy Lloyd’s message to Tucson: “We all saw what’s possible again. So now let’s all roll up our sleeves and support each other and see if we can make this a normal thing.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCadeau on dome shooting issues Imagn ImagesAdd Elliot Cadeau to the depth perception discussion of basketball games in football stadiums:💬 “I think it kind of takes a little time to get used to shooting at game speed in this arena.”Don't count out UConnTommy Lloyd on people saying tonight’s Michigan-Arizona matchup was a de facto championship game: “Listen, I don’t think anybody is going to count UConn out. So that’s why when everybody was saying this is the national championship game, it’s not the national championship game. Monday night is the national championship game, and you have to fight to get there. So, yeah, credit to Michigan. Really impressive tonight.” Imagn ImagesDusty May on Yaxel Lendeborg returning to finish tonight's Final Four game: 💬 “The guys know that Yax is about winning.”A big takeaway from tonight’s game is the sheer importance of experience, particularly in March. Tommy Lloyd was asked about that, given the lack of experience from his Arizona stars.💬 “I don’t think it was inexperience today. We had a good couple of days of practice. We had a good shoot-around today. I think we just came out, and we played a team that was really well built. They have a great coach. They were able to take control of the game, and then really, they were like surgical at a point.”Lendeborg draws praise from his teammates Imagn ImagesYaxel Lendeborg was going to return to play in the second half of the game despite his MCL sprain and ankle sprain. He turned to his family and friends during the game to say so, yelling, “I have to, I have to.” He confirmed to CBS Sports’ Tracy Wolfson that he’s going to play in Monday’s national championship game against UConn no matter what: “I’m going to play unless I can’t walk at all.”His teammates, Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney, sang their star forward praises for his resilience.Cadeau: 💬 “We know what type of guy Yaxel is, if he can play, he’s going to play. We asked him, ‘Are you good?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ So we expect him to be on the court. He told us when he got on the court, he was going to give it his all.”McKenney: 💬 “I think it just shows the guy who Yaxel is. I mean, he just wants to put it all on the floor for Michigan, and he wants to give the fans what they came here for. I’m just really grateful to have him as a teammate. He’s one of the best players in the country. He really showed that tonight. But he’s selfless as well. So I’m just really grateful to be around him.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCredit to LloydGot to credit Tommy Lloyd for the way he’s handled this loss. Speaking to Tracy Wolfson immediately after an 18-point loss in the Final Four, Lloyd gave Michigan all the credit and took accountability.At his postgame news conference, Lloyd said: “Michigan gets all the credit today.”He added: “It wasn’t our night, probably had a lot to do with them. They were just impressive. They were impressive how they came out and executed their game plan. And we got down a little bit, and we’ve been down a few times this year, but not like that. Just probably got a little panicky and weren’t able to settle back in. And they get credit. That’s why if you can get off to a good start in games, you know, it’s usually pretty impactful. That definitely was the case today.”Strong 3-point shooting a common theme Getty ImagesDespite playing in Lucas Oil Stadium, UConn and Michigan used 3-point shooting to build insurmountable leads in their respective semifinal victories.Both teams tallied 12 3-pointers in their respective wins, with the Huskies' total setting a new program record for an NCAA Tournament game. UConn accomplished the feat in 33 attempts, while Michigan took only 27 attempts to reach a dozen treys.Keep an eye on long-range attempts from Michigan's Trey McKenney, Elliot Cadeau and Yaxel Lendeborg and UConn's Braylon Mullens and Solo Ball, each who recorded at least three 3-point makes today.Bradley on his time at ArizonaSenior point guard Jaden Bradley on what his three years at Arizona (he was at Alabama his freshman year) meant to him:💬 “It means a lot. I appreciate Coach Lloyd and the staff for taking me in and giving me, I’d like to say, like a fresh start. I appreciate this team. We accomplished a lot this year. We definitely wanted to win this game, but Michigan was a better team tonight. Appreciate Tucson. Just love this group. Cherish the last couple gatherings we have together before everybody goes their own ways, but just happy to be a part of this team.”May: Michigan's performance reflected its identity Getty ImagesMichigan head coach Dusty May’s opening statement after his Wolverines throttled Arizona 91-73, equalling the largest men’s NCAA Tournament win between two No. 1 seeds:💬 “This game was very indicative of how this group has played throughout the season, unselfish basketball. A connected group who defends, gets out in transition and then shares the basketball.“I thought our assist-to-turnover ratio, I thought our job on the glass, especially before the game was not in doubt and is as impressive as anything and but the one thing that we thought really jumped out was our ability to get 50/50 basketballs and be quicker to the ball than Arizona tonight, but just very proud of our effort. What a great group.”Lloyd on Arizona's loss Getty Images Tommy Lloyd’s opening statement after a season-ending defeat to Michigan in the Final Four:💬 “First off, I want to thank the players on our team and the staff. They were amazing this year, and it was an awesome, awesome journey. It was as much fun as I’ve ever had coaching basketball.“Secondly, I want to give credit to Michigan. I mean, they were outstanding tonight. Really had us on our heels tonight. We never could get in a rhythm. So they get a ton of credit for that. No one’s been able to do that to us all year. So it was an impressive performance by them.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMcKenney lights it up Getty ImagesWith Yaxel Lendeborg limited and Elliot Cadeau cold from the field, Trey McKenney stepped up as a human sparkplug for Michigan off the bench. McKenney had the hot hand, going 6-for-9 from the field and 4-for-6 from 3-point range. His 16 points were second on the team, to only Aday Mara's 26.More on Mara Imagn ImagesDusty May says he and the Michigan staff watched Aday Mara's Spanish national team tape and Zaragoza tape as much as his UCLA tape when evaluating him out of the transfer portal last summer:💬 “He had shown glimpses of this. ... But he's playing ball at a high level, and he's adding a lot to our program.” Lindsay Schnell / The AthleticYaxel hasn't had an MRI yet. He said the trainers told him it's likely an MCL sprain. He plans to get an MRI later tonight or tomorrow.First look at Monday nightThe stage is set. UConn and Michigan will play for the national championship in men’s basketball on Monday night in Indianapolis.The No. 2-seeded Huskies, seeking a third title in four seasons, dispatched No. seed 3 Illinois 71-62. Top-seeded Michigan routed fellow No. 1 Arizona 91-73, adding a fourth blowout win to its five-game run through this NCAA Tournament.The results on Saturday ensured a historic result in the title game. No program has won three championships in four years since John Wooden’s UCLA teams more than years ago. And it’s been longer than a quarter-century since a Big Ten team — Michigan State in 2000 — hoisted the trophy.May defends choice to allow Lendeborg to return to game Imagn ImagesDusty May on why he brought Yaxel Lendeborg back late in the second half with Michigan’s seemingly guaranteed:💬 “Well, apparently, you guys missed the UConn-Duke game. The game was already decided, and we were playing Duke tomorrow. They were up 19, correct, in the second half? And who won?“So being out — you’re playing Arizona, one of the best teams, statistically, the No. 1 or 2 team all year in the country, you’re up with 20 with 10 minutes left, with eight and a half minutes left. We didn’t feel quite as confident as you guys did that we could just put the kids to bed. And he came in and Elliot (Cadeau) was in foul trouble, and so he just held it down.“So yeah, obviously we felt like the game was still in hand.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCadeau was superb Getty ImagesElliot Cadeau had one of the best 5-for-17 shooting nights you will ever see.Cadeau had a 13-point, 10-assist double-double and impacted the game in just about every facet. Arizona’s talented backcourt of Jaden Bradley and Brayden Burries had no answer for how to deal with Cadeau’s defense, and Cadeau recorded four steals on his own. His passing, as evidenced by his 10 assists, was superb — and needed, as he and Aday Mara both stepped up as facilitators as Yaxel Lendeborg dealt with foul and injury trouble.Some of Cadeau's misses ... were intentional?Fascinating: Dusty May says that Michigan actually spent time the last few days practicing throwing passes off the backboard, to help mitigate some of the rim protection that Arizona center Mo Krivas presented. Said that, yes, Elliot Cadeau was 2-of-14 shooting in the first half, but a couple of those "shots" were actually passes off the backboard in line with what UM had practiced.All smiles for Michigan duoQuite the buddy-comedy dynamic for Dusty May and his leading scorer tonight Aday Mara, as our Justin Williams highlights below.When was Michigan's last men's basketball title? Getty ImagesIn contrast to UConn — a program that is hoping to win its third title in four years — the Michigan Wolverines will enter the national championship with the opportunity to end a championship drought spanning decades.Michigan's last national championship win came in the 1989 tournament, when the Wolverines edged Seton Hall 80-79 in overtime.The Wolverines appeared in the national championship game in 1992, 1993, 2013 and 2018 but lost all four games.Lendeborg: 'No way I'm missing' national title gameYaxel Lendeborg to Tracy Wolfson postgame, speaking on his injuries: 💬 “I mean, it’s (laughs) to have a weird feeling to have the pain that I’m having right now, never experienced it before, so — Coach said at worst, MCL sprain, and then obviously I rolled my ankle so I mean just that. Imma push through, there’s no way I’m missing the game Monday night. I’m going to play unless I can’t walk at all.”On the key Monday night vs. UConn: 💬 “It’s gonna take a full 40 minutes of fighting and bringing our best effort, you know, we have the squad to do it, we all love each other and that plays a big part in games like Monday night, so we’re gonna do the best we can and the Fab Five is here so we’re gonna do the best (for?) those guys too.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementRout sends Michigan to Monday nightStyles make fights, and this had all the makings of a heavyweight bout.The two best teams in college basketball. Two of the tallest, toughest and most physical rosters, embodying the sport’s big-ball takeover this season. But it was Michigan that came out swinging and immediately had Arizona on the ropes, setting the tone for a 91-73 victory to send the Wolverines to the national championship game against UConn on Monday.When was the last time a Big Ten team won it all? Getty ImagesLike UCLA attempting to become the first Big Ten team since 1999 to win the women's NCAA Tournament tomorrow, Michigan will look to end a title drought for the Big Ten on the men's side.The last Big Ten team to run the table in the NCAA Tournament was the Michigan State Spartans in 2000.May heaps praise on UConn Getty ImagesDusty May to Tracy Wolfson postgame:💬 “I wanna give a shoutout to our glue guys, they really held it in the road and in the first half when we were battling foul trouble and some injuries. We were able to get some stops and we were able to get out in transition and get a little separation.”“Obviously you have to be ultra-competitive as a group to be here. But our basketball IQ and team intelligence is why we’re still playing.”May was seen scouting during the UConn-Illinois game before his team took on Illinois. Wolfson asked him about it:💬 “They have championship DNA. What they’ve done over the last four years is as impressive as anything we’ve seen. We got our hands full Monday, but these guys will be up for the challenge.”National championship finalists have contrasting paths Getty ImagesLike their respective semifinal games today, UConn and Michigan have had drastically different styles of victory in their NCAA Tournament runs.UConn's buzzer-beater to upset Duke was the game of the tournament, but the Huskies also had close calls after holding commanding leads early against Michigan State in the Sweet 16 and Illinois today.Michigan hasn't had to sweat out a game yet. The Wolverines have scored 90 points in each of their five games and have won each game by at least 13 points.UConn's style certainly leads to more entertaining finishes, but regardless of their respective paths, the two teams will be a must-see matchup Monday night.Fab Five loving it Getty ImagesThe Fab Five, from their perches doing a live watch-along, gestured their appreciation to the shout-out Yaxel Lendeborg gave them in his postgame interview.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementChampionship matchup set Getty ImagesMichigan advances to Monday night's championship game and will face UConn. The tipoff is scheduled for 8:30 p.m. ET.Michigan will try to win its second national title. UConn its seventh.Mara was magnificent Justin Williams / The AthleticCareer-high 26 points for this big fella.He also hd nine rebounds and three assists. Shot 11-of-16 from the field.Final stats breakdown from Michigan-Arizona Getty ImagesIn a battle of No. 1 seeds, Michigan cruised past Arizona to advance to the national championship. Here are the final team stats from today's clash:FG:Michigan: 33-69Arizona: 26-713FG:Michigan: 12-27Arizona: 6-17Rebounds:Michigan: 40Arizona: 44Assists:Michigan: 22Arizona: 5Turnovers:Michigan: 13Arizona: 14Points in the paint:Michigan: 36Arizona: 36Largest lead:Michigan: 30Arizona: 0Lendeborg scores 11 despite leaving with injuryEven with the Wolverines maintaining a comfortable lead throughout the second half, Yaxel Lendeborg demonstrated his physical and mental grit by playing through his left ankle injury to start the second half, and again in the final minutes.Should Lendeborg have been in the game when Michigan was already cruising, and he risked re-injuring his ankle? Ultimately, Lendeborg finished his performance without re-aggravating the injury, and he’ll have another chance to suit up for the Wolverines on Monday. His final stat line: 11 points, 3-of-3 on 3-point shooting and three rebounds in 14 minutes of action.Scoring leaders from Michigan-Arizona Getty ImagesScoring leaders from Michigan's commanding victory over Arizona:Michigan: Aday Mara (26 points, 11-16 FG)Arizona: Koa Peat (14 points, 5-17 FG)SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFINAL: Michigan rolls past Arizona! Getty ImagesFINAL - Michigan 91, Arizona 73That’s it!Utter domination from the Wolverines against a very, very good Arizona team. What a statement in the Final Four!Three years after his FAU team got its heart broken on a Final Four buzzer beater, Dusty May has taken a team to the national title game for a matchup with UConn!Michigan vs. UConn, Monday night for all the marbles.Lendeborg updateYaxel Lendeborg has a pretty big wrap on his left knee now, but is all smiles on the bench.Michigan finally empties its bench, including Charlie May. UConn vs. Michigan it shall be.H2 0:50 - Michigan 90, Arizona 73Now Dusty May pulls the remainder of his starters.Among the substitutions now on the floor for Michigan... Charlie May, Dusty’s son.Mara shows his value to Michigan Getty ImagesYaxel Lendeborg was the Big Ten player of the year, but for my money, Aday Mara is the catalyst for Michigan. He does so much on both ends to make the Wolverines, as he showed tonight with 26 points and seven rebounds. Assuming Lendeborg will be limited Monday night, expect Michigan to play through Mara once again.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty ImagesH2 2:24 - Michigan 90, Arizona 71The only blemish on any Michigan player’s stat line tonight is their fouls. Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney each have four, and Aday Mara just picked up his third. Not that it will have any impact on the game at this point. Getty ImagesFor those interested, tonight's attendance was 72,111. A lot of empty seats now though and WAY less orange than when the day began.The biggest comeback in Final Four history, if you're curious ...That would be 22 points, Duke over Maryland in the 2001 national semifinals ... the last time Arizona was in the Final Four.Pull the starters, DustyThis game has gotten a bit chippy late. It's time for Michigan to empty its bench and move on to Monday. Getty Images'Biggest comeback in March Madness history' is currently trending in search. Wildcat fans haven't given up hope, even if it's a long shot.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty ImagesH2 4:22 - Michigan 86, Arizona 64Yaxel Lendeborg is back out of the game out of a brief return. The biggest issue for Michigan, for the second straight game, is to avoid any extracurriculars here as Morez Johnson Jr. had to be separated from Brayden Burries after talking some trash.Even the alerts are shading Arizona A less kind thing you can say about this game, from the official March Madness app...More on Lendeborg's returnAccording to Tracy Wolfson, Yaxel Lendeborg turned to his family and friends and said, “I have to, I have to,” and then checked back into the game despite dealing with an MCL sprain on his knee and an ankle injury, and Michigan up double digits.H2 5:19 - Michigan 86, Arizona 64As Michael said, Yaxel Lendeborg is inexplicably back in this game. Anyway, Michigan has maintained a 20-point lead and Aday Mara is up to an impressive 25 points after a TOUGH and-1 on Koa Peat.Lendeborg back in Imagn ImagesAs this game winds down all eyes will be on the health of Yaxel Lendeborg, who just checked into the game for some reason?SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementA friend just texted me, "When Bear Down turns to beat down ..." and you know what, it's one of the kinder things you can say about Arizona and this game.Full circle for Dusty May Getty ImagesH2 7:33 - Michigan 81, Arizona 60To Chris’s point earlier, Dusty May’s Florida Atlantic tenure was highlighted by the Owls’ run to the Final Four as a No. 9 seed in 2023. Only Lamont Butler’s buzzer-beater for San Diego State prevented FAU from playing for the national championship that year.Three years later, May is finally about to head to the title game, where he’ll face the same opponent his FAU team would have faced in 2023 — Dan Hurley’s UConn Huskies.A coach's son in the Final Four?Speaking of which, did someone just fire up the Charlie May signal? It's almost that time.H2 8:23 - Michigan 81, Arizona 58The broadcast camera keeps cutting to newly minted Hall of Famer Mark Few, who does not look thrilled as his longtime assistant, protege and good friend Tommy Lloyd is getting a rude welcome to his first Final Four as a head coach.May solidifies himself as an elite coach Getty ImagesWinners win and Dusty May wins. He’s 123-26 with two Final Fours and a Sweet 16 over the last four years at FAU and Michigan.FAU had five winning seasons in its history, then he arrived and had six winning seasons in six years. Michigan went 8-23 the year before he got there. Now he has the Wolverines in the national title game in year two.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Getty ImagesH2 10:18 - Michigan 77, Arizona 49Michigan is shooting 48 percent from 3-point range.Arizona is shooting 37 percent from the field.Yeah.Worth the wait for Cadeau Getty ImagesElliot Cadeau has his first double double of the tournament at 11 points and 10 assists. It’s his third of the season.They are playing Mr. Brightside in Indy to the delight of the Michigan faithful. Imagn ImagesFantastic sight to see Yaxel Lendeborg out there, looking just fine before subbing out.Gronk smiles through the painBoos for Rob Gronkowski, who just smiles and flexes in true Gronk fashion.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFormer Arizona football player Rob Gronkowski is here in an Arizona jersey. Can he sub in? Maybe he can slow down Aday Mara.A Wolverine celebration Getty ImagesYaxel Lendeborg received a massive ovation from the Wolverine fans as he checked out. It's become a party for Michigan here in the second half. Moments later, Elliot Cadeau cans consecutive triples and celebrates boisterously toward his bench. Michigan can smell a championship game appearance.Why Lendeborg returned Getty ImagesTracy Wolfson said Michigan head athletic trainer Chris Williams and the team’s doctor ...“Cleared Yaxel to play and put it up to Yaxel himself whether he wanted to go back out there, which he did.”H2 12:17 - Michigan 72, Arizona 45As if the Wolverines needed any other yelp, Elliot Cadeau has finally gotten going with his shooting stroke! Back-to-back triples gives him 11 points on 4-of-16 shooting, but he’s been so impactful out there in every other way... as evidenced by his 10 (!!!) assists, four rebounds and three steals.Tommy Lloyd calls timeout. He may as well wave a white flag. Getty ImagesUp 21, Yaxel Lenderborg finally limps out for Michigan.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementOfficials warn Mara Getty ImagesAfter that last dunk, hang and flex by Mara, one of the officials said something to Dusty May on the way back down floor, with May quickly relaying the "cut it out" signal to Mara.Trey McKenney is on a heater, folks Getty ImagesH2 13:02 - Michigan 66, Arizona 44Trey McKenney! Another 3-pointer with Koa Peat’s hand in his face, which followed an Aday Mara flush off an alley-oop and an McKenney stepback at the elbow.McKenney has 13 off the bench. It’s a 22-point Michigan lead.Just utter domination.Peat struggling against Michigan Getty ImagesKoa Peat not exactly assuaging pro scouts' fears about how he would fare against NBA size without a threatening jump shot. Getty ImagesThe score isn't the same (yet), but this game has major Gonzaga-Michigan vibes in terms of how thoroughly Michigan is dominating and how shellshocked Arizona looks.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementLendeborg's mom loving itYissel Raposo is having a blast in the stands as her son, Yaxel Lendeborg, just drained back-to-back triples, and his Wolverines are having a blast in this Final Four, up 56-34 to top-seeded Arizona.For a beautiful look into Lendeborg and Raposo’s very special relationship, do take a read of Justin Williams’ feature from this week. Getty ImagesH2 15:40 - Michigan 56, Arizona 39A little 5-0 run for the Wildcats into the media timeout, and they’re still down 17.With Yaxel Lendeborg clearly hobbled but splashing 3s anyway, Arizona is running out of options quickly.Yaxel Lendeborg out here like Greg Jennings, splashing 3s on one leg.Everything coming up MichiganHere's five-star guard Brandon McCoy, the No. 11 player in nation, telling the Fab Five he plans to play at Michigan next year. This night couldn't be going much better for the Wolverines. Getty ImagesThis game has turned into a contested layup contest for some reason — until Lendeborg hit ANOTHER 3.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMore on Lendeborg Getty ImagesTracy Wolfson says Michigan head athletic trainer Chris Williams told her that Yaxel Lendeborg is dealing with an MCL sprain of his left knee and an ankle injury. Was given ice and a massage in the locker room, and an active warmup, before he started the second half.Getting late early Getty ImagesRemember how I said the first five minutes are important? Well, Jaden Bradley picked up his fourth foul in the first two minutes. I know there's a lot of time left, but this is close to game over,And on that note, why on earth is Yaxel Lendeborg playing right now? Getty ImagesArizona needs to attack Yaxel Lendeborg and make him defend in space. He was not moving well during warmups.So far, no success for the Wildcats on the offensive end.Lendeborg looked very limited changing ends on these first two trips; he usually flies up and down the court. Getty ImagesH2 17:45 - Michigan 53, Arizona 32WOW. After a lob to Aday Mara starts the scoring, a clearly limited Yaxel Lendeborg hits a 3!SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMy thought on starting Yaxel is… why? Michigan’s in control, there’s little need right now.H2 18:26 - Michigan 48, Arizona 32A lid on both baskets to start the second half, which obviously favors Michigan...And Jaden Bradley promptly picks up his fourth foul.Lendeborg on the court Getty ImagesFirst five minutes of the second half are gonna be huge, and likely dictate the rest of the game. Yaxel Lendeborg starting the second half.Lendeborg out on the court for second half Justin Williams / The AthleticYaxel Lendeborg is out walking on his toes and jogging at halftime, with the team athletic trainer looking on intently. The fact that he's out and moving around is a good sign, but he's definitely moving gingerly. At this point, the Wolverines probably don't need him. Sit him down for the second half and try to get him right for Monday.Reader views on first halfBelow are your first-half reader views, featuring a lot of enthusiastic Michigan fans. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAfter the Purdue game, Jaden Bradley told me the Wildcats were able to come back and win after a 7-point halftime deficit partially because they just pretended they were ahead, figuring it would help them relax. I'm not sure that strategy will work tonight.Michigan winning on and off the court right nowOn the bright side for Michigan, they just landed 5-star prospect Brandon McCoy Jr.McCoy was a McDonald's All American who chose the Wolverines over Arkansas, Miami and Alabama.Wolverines on a roll Getty ImagesLast week, Michigan was up 48-26 on Tennessee at halftime in the Elite Eight. Tonight, the Wolverines are up 48-32 at the half against Arizona. Just complete dominance by Michigan.Michigan leads Arizona in assists 12-2 Getty ImagesRe-upping my point from earlier, Arizona really did follow in Illinois’ footsteps, finishing this half with just two assists (the Illini had one). Michigan had 12, much like UConn, the eventual winner in the first semifinal, had nine heading into intermission.Cadeau on Michigan's aggression Getty ImagesHere’s what Michigan guard Elliot Cadeau had to say at halftime about how his team set the tone in the first half:💬 “Just really aggressive. I came out aggressive offensively. Even though my shot wasn't falling, I stayed with it. And we’re gonna continue to keep that mindset in the second half. ... If we got the best player in the country (Yaxel Lendeborg), it’s good for us, if we don’t, we’ve still got a really good team.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementIs Michigan rolling toward another rout? Getty ImagesMichigan leads Arizona by 16 points at halftime. Is another blowout in the works?Here are Michigan's margins of victory so far in the tournament:First round against Howard: 31 pointsSecond round against Saint Louis: 23 pointsSweet 16 against Alabama: 23 pointsElite Eight against Tennessee: 33 pointsMichigan flexing depth Getty ImagesDusty May played nine guys for a lot of this season, a deeper rotation than a lot of coaches want to play. Elliot Cadeau just said it on TV — the Wolverines feel like they have nine starters. It's a big reason they've been able to withstand the injury to L.J. Cason and now the absence of Yaxel Lendeborg to be 20 minutes from a trip to the national championship game.Wildcats do not look like a No. 1 seed Getty ImagesThe score is 48-32, but it feels like Arizona is down 30. Wildcats aren't doing anything that got them here, not owning the paint, not dominating the boards, not getting to the line (and when they do, not making foul shots).Inexperience showing for Arizona Getty ImagesA lesson from this NCAA Tournament is once again that freshmen are still freshmen. Veterans are still often winning out in March. Arizona’s star frosh have really struggled tonight.Michigan's supporting cast stepping up Getty ImagesMichigan is destroying Arizona, with basically nothing from its best player — which of course could loom large Monday — and with a 2-for-14 showing so far from Elliot Cadeau, who I swear is still playing a great game. Non-Cadeau Wolverines are 15-for-29.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementArizona getting taste of own medicine Getty ImagesArizona has won all season by being more physical, more defensive-minded, more intense, more resilient, and Michigan has been better in every category.Cadeau on missing LendeborgElliot Cadeau on playing without Yaxel Lendeborg: 💬 “We got another man that can step up. We got nine starters on our team, so if we got the best player in the country, it’s good for us; if we don’t, we still got a really good team.”Keep an eye out for Lendeborg's return Getty ImagesIn an otherwise sterling first half by the Michigan Wolverines, Yaxel Lendeborg's leaving for the locker room was a concerning development.Lendeborg left the game in the first half after re-aggravating the left ankle injury that sidelined him in the Big Ten tournament. He left for the locker room, then returned to the court, only to return to the locker room to further address the ankle.Even with a substantial lead, Michigan will hope to use Lendeborg to close out the No. 1-seeded Wildcats in the second half.Mara showing what his old UCLA team is missingDusty May has utilized Aday Mara so, so well, and much better than Mara’s previous coach, Mick Cronin at UCLA, did. Mara averaged just 13 minutes last season in Westwood and now gets 23 minutes per game for the Wolverines.
